title: A session in its own copy can be forked into a new copy
request: Open gap from the owner's list: forking a session that works in its own copy was refused. Owner: continue non-stop.
plan: check the agent resumes a fork from another folder
fork into a new copy from the branch

decisions.decision: the fork gets its own new copy from the original copy's branch tip, merging into the same base
decisions.why: two sessions must never share a folder; Claude Code's desktop app forks the same way (commit first, uncommitted edits stay)

decisions.decision: uncommitted changes are named in the fork's note, not refused
decisions.why: the person may want the fork anyway; saying what stays behind is enough
the SDK files a conversation under the folder it ran in; forkSession has no target folder

findings.defect: risk: a forked conversation might not resume in the new copy's folder
findings.scenario: forkSession writes under the original's folder; the fork runs in another
findings.fix: none needed: measured that resume finds it from any folder (a made-up id fails)
findings.test: SDK probe without an API key; live PELICAN check

findings.defect: the live script read the fork's copied history as its answer
findings.scenario: waiting for a result in the fork's records
findings.cause: a fork's records begin with the original's copied results

measurements.name: tests
measurements.result: 147 of 147 (the refusal test replaced by a fork-into-copy test: committed file comes, uncommitted stays and is named, removed copy refused)

measurements.name: live, Haiku 5.5
measurements.gate: the fork in its new copy remembers the original's conversation

outcome: Fork works for every session; a fork of a copy session works in its own new copy.
lessons: Probe the SDK's behaviour without an API key before designing around a guess.
A fork's records start with copies: count only its own.
